Three vendors have a signed DPA: Parcelwise, Saltmarsh Analytics, and Cobaltline. Hollowpine Helpdesk does not.

- **Parcelwise Ltd.** (transactional email): signed November 20, 2023, amended September 2025 for EU standard contractual clauses [1].
- **Saltmarsh Analytics GmbH** (product analytics): signed June 12, 2025 [2].
- **Cobaltline, Inc.** (log search and retention): signed April 2, 2025 [3].
- **Hollowpine Software Co.** (support ticketing): not signed. The DPA draft arrived in July 2026, and redlines with legal have been open since August. The main open point is Hollowpine's right to use ticket content to train its reply-suggestion model [4]. It is operating under security exception SEC-EX-117, approved August 24, 2026 [4]. AI reply suggestions must stay disabled until the DPA is signed [4]. The exception needs renewing or Support must move ticket intake back to email if the DPA is still unsigned when it lapses [4].

These four were the only vendor records my search returned, so if you have other vendors, check their register entries directly.

Cycle 5 picked three big bets: **Tributary**, **Lantern**, and **Hydrant** [1].

- **Tributary:** streaming joins (the Enrich step in the pipeline editor), led by Lin Zhou. It was pitched by Mateo and LZ [1][4]. Private beta started October 1 with eight design partners, and GA stays January 2027 [4][5]. Security sign-off on persisted snapshots is still outstanding and is the main risk [5].
- **Lantern:** a self-serve billing portal where customers manage invoices, plans, payment methods, and usage reports. It was pitched by NH and HV [1]. Its timeline has moved. The pitch targeted a December beta and January 2027 GA [1], but the October leadership notes and the project register now show a February 2027 beta and March 2027 GA [4][5]. The slip is tied to the payment-provider migration, which won't finish until mid-January, and to invoice-history work for voided invoices [5].
- **Hydrant:** automatic scaling of ingest gateways per cell, pitched by OA [1]. It has shipped to all production cells as of October 22, 2026 [3].

The pitch review also added small batch items, including the gateway TLS session ticket change from INC-2291 [1]. Tidepool (Postgres CDC v2) was not picked in cycle 5 and is slated for a re-pitch with smaller scope [4].

Four endpoints return HTTP 403 on Starter, so Starter workspaces can't use them at all:

- `POST /v2/events/batch` (bulk backfill and replays) [1]
- `POST /v2/reference-tables/{id}/refresh` (forces an Enrich snapshot rebuild) [1]
- `GET /v2/audit-log/export` (audit log CSV export) [1]
- `/v2/scim/*` (SCIM user provisioning) [1]

The rate-limit table marks these as "Not available" for Starter. Those requests fail with HTTP 403, not HTTP 429 [1]. The source doesn't say whether the audit log export is restricted for Starter in the product UI, so the table is the only evidence I have. The other Starter endpoints are available but limited, such as `POST /v2/events` at 100 req/s [1].

| `runner` | Executes customer pipelines (transforms, Enrich steps, destinations) [1] | DP [1] |
| Conduit | Source and destination connectors such as Postgres, MySQL, Snowflake and warehouses [1] | DP [1] |
| Driftwood | Long-term object archive behind the hot buffer [1] | PLAT [1] |
| Keystone | Authentication and authorization for the app and API [1] | IDB [1] |

Restricted data is defined as customer event payloads, credentials and encryption keys, and it never leaves production [2]. Normal changes to these services also need sign-off from the Head of Security or the security on-call delegate [3].

**Four languages missed their connect-time target on average in Q3 2026 (July 1 to September 30):** Vietnamese, Arabic, Somali, and Karen.

- **Arabic** (2-minute tier): average 2:12 [1]
- **Somali** (5-minute tier): average 5:40 [1]
- **Karen** (5-minute tier): average 6:18 [1]

The report compares averages against the targets: 2 minutes for the top 20 languages and American Sign Language, and 5 minutes for all others [1]. Because it reports averages, some individual sessions in these languages may have met the target. The "all other languages (61)" row is aggregated at 3:31, so the report can't show whether any single language in that group missed [1].

Clinical Operations plans to raise every language that missed its target at the Polyglen renewal discussion in November 2026 [1]. Separately, it wants to move Haitian Creole and Karen into the 2-minute tier [2].

- **Meningococcal B vaccine** (0.5 mL prefilled syringe), self-pay $190 per dose. Ages 16–23 or on specialist advice [1].

Any item not on the formulary at all cannot be given in clinic without approval from the Pharmacy and Therapeutics subcommittee [1].

Under the current standard (effective September 1, 2026), a clinic is large if its average is over 80 in-person visits per day [1]. Based on the Q3 2026 averages in the clinic directory, three clinics qualify:

- Harbor Point (HBP): 118 visits per day [3]
- Northgate (NGT): 102 visits per day [3]
- Riverside (RVS): 94 visits per day [3]

Elm Park (ELP) is at 85, which puts it in the large band as well [3]. That makes four large clinics: Harbor Point, Northgate, Riverside, and Elm Park.

The other clinics are medium (40 to 80) or small (under 40) [1][3]. Northbridge (52) and Riverbend (46) are medium. Elmhurst (38) and Cedar Hollow (31) are small.

Bands are reset every quarter from the visit column, so these may change [1][3]. The 2025 standard used a different threshold of over 90, which would have counted only Harbor Point, Northgate and Riverside [2].

Five vendors offer 24/7 support that covers P1 problems:

| Vendor | System | P1 response | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Meridian Clinical Systems | Meridian EHR | 15 minutes | 24/7 for all priorities [1] |
| ClearPath Software | ClearPath PM | 30 minutes | 24/7 for P1 only; other issues are 07:00–19:00 Eastern, Mon–Fri [1] |
| Coriander Media | Video SDK and hosted media servers | 20 minutes | 24/7 [1] |
| Bayline Reference Laboratories | HL7 results feed into Switchyard | 30 minutes | 24/7 interface desk [1] |
| Polyglen Interpreting | Interpreter operations desk | 10 minutes | 24/7. P1 covers an interpreter not connecting at all [1][2] |

The other vendors on the matrix do not provide round-the-clock support:
- Larkspur Telehealth covers 07:00–21:00 Eastern, 7 days a week [1].
- Quillon Ambient (AI scribe pilot) covers 06:00–22:00 Eastern, Mon–Sat. It has no out-of-hours P1 line, so clinicians document manually [1].
- RotaLeaf covers 08:00–18:00 Eastern, Mon–Fri [1].

Halcyon's in-house systems have no outside vendor. The Service Desk pages the owning team directly for those [1].
